To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the finite section method converges to the pseudo-spectra of pseudoergodic operators, (b) the convergence is faster when using periodic boundary conditions and (c) this is a general result that applies to any dimension.
the finite section approximation of pseudoergodic operators converges to their pseudospectra, and that periodic boundary conditions are often a better choice than uneven sections.
the finite section with periodic boundary conditions is a convergent method for computing the pseudospectrum and the method of uneven section is convergent for pseudoergodic operators.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the convergence of the finite section method for non-self-adjont operators with periodic boundary conditions and its relation to pseudospectra, and the numerical implications of this convergence.
the numerical computation of the pseudospectrum for a large class of infinite operators and provides an algorithm that is numerically stable and convergent.
the numerical computation of the pseudospectrum (and not the spectrum) of pseudoergodic operators and the use of periodic boundary conditions to achieve convergence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
pseudoergodic operators are pseudospectrally stable under periodic boundary conditions, but not under Dirichlet boundary conditions, which is the case for self-adjoint operators.
the finite section methods with periodic boundary conditions converge to pseudospectra of the full operator for a wide class of operators, including the case of pseudoergodic operators.
the finite section with periodic boundary conditions is a robust and reliable numerical method for the pseudospectra of pseudoergodic operators.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the finite section with periodic boundary conditions is a convergent method for the pseudospectra of pseudoergodic operators.
the finite section approximation of pseudoergodic operators is convergent in the p-norm to the pseudospectra of the full operator, and the convergence is faster with periodic boundary conditions.
the finite section approximation with periodic boundary conditions is a robust method for approximating the pseudospectrum.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the finite section approximation with periodic boundary conditions is a good approximation for the pseudospectra of a pseudoergodic operator, and thus a good tool to understand the stability of a system.
the pseudospectral behaviour of pseudoergodic operators is better captured by finite sections with periodic boundary conditions than the classical finite sections.
